obligations.criterion: An excitation binds a signal to physical space and declares: stable excitation identity and containing excitation-case identity; typed action such as force, moment, traction, pressure, body force, base displacement/velocity/acceleration, heat generation, heat flux, ambient temperature, current density, terminal voltage, acoustic pressure, normal velocity, inlet velocity, or mass flow; persistent region, entity, reference-point, port, or interface target; coordinate frame, direction, components, and follower/non-follower behavior where meaningful; distribution and normalization policy, including whether an authored resultant or an intensity is preserved; active procedure steps and combination group; associated signal or field artifact; and projection and conservation requirements. Realization produces immutable topology- and operator-compatible data. It records resolved entities, quadrature/integration policy, resultant and moment checks, units, signal digest, projection digest, and any interpolation or transfer error. Mesh-dependent generated spatial fields are materialized after topology projection and before assembly. They may be partitioned preprocessing work, but never callbacks inside element quadrature or a solver iteration.

RunMat code may construct a signal from ordinary arrays or from a function handle or anonymous closure. Array construction is the simplest path and naturally composes with RunMat signal processing, control systems, data access, sparse values, parallel execution, and GPU placement. A callable-backed constructor additionally requires a typed domain and materialization policy. The preferred callable is vectorized over time, frequency, parameter, or canonical sample points. Before the solve: resolve the callable through the normal typed callable system; validate its declared input/output facts and captures; freeze its source project or compiled package closure; reject unsupported effects and capabilities; evaluate it in a bounded preprocessing task; validate shape, quantity, units, finiteness, domain coverage, and continuity claims; materialize a canonical signal or field artifact; and make the solver depend only on that artifact. Adaptive time stepping does not justify a live solver callback. A generator is adaptively sampled ahead of the solve to a declared interpolation tolerance, with discontinuities represented by explicit breakpoints or step interpolation. If a prescribed kinematic history is supplied as displacement, the materializer must receive or deterministically derive compatible velocity and acceleration and record derivative-error evidence. A direct base-acceleration history does not require artificial integration to displacement unless the selected formulation needs it.

The initial production effect policy rejects workspace writes, environment mutation, undeclared filesystem access, network access, UI interaction, uncontrolled randomness, clock dependence, host callbacks, and unknown effects. Immutable portable captures are allowed. Random excitation uses an explicit seed, distribution, PSD/cross-PSD, or frozen realization. Session-bound handles, mutable handle objects, foreign references, and unfenced device handles are rejected. The intended language shape is ordinary numerical preparation followed by a small number of typed FEA constructors. Exact names should follow the builtin/object conventions present after platform convergence, but the semantic shape is: The callable form describes how to produce the same typed history; it does not change what the solver receives: Quantity-specific convenience constructors use documented canonical units. A general constructor, if exposed, requires explicit typed time/frequency axes and dimensioned values; it must not accept an unqualified numeric array plus a free-form quantity string. Typed direction, frame, interpolation, extrapolation, response measure, and combination-policy values replace solver-layer string dispatch.

A data-only `.fea` remains fully standalone. It may contain bounded inline samples or reference a declared data object that is content-hashed and frozen into the study bundle. The declarative form resolves once into the same typed objects. It imports the generating function from its actual `.m` file rather than relying on a magic namespace: Base acceleration is prescribed support kinematics rather than an ordinary excitation. It must identify the support region, driven degree of freedom, initial displacement and velocity, and the governed reconstruction. The referenced acceleration history is a real global vector over time; ordinary forces and source terms continue to use the excitation contract. A code-generated input references an explicitly imported project function plus typed arguments and sampling/materialization policy. It does not embed source text, a live closure, an absolute host path, or base-workspace state. `runmat run study.fea` resolves the enclosing RunMat project, freezes the same source graph and callable inventory used by ordinary program execution, and includes it in the encrypted execution bundle. Without a resolvable project and callable, planning fails before expensive work begins. An explicit relative `.m` import resolves immediately to a project-owned qualified function identity. Package-qualified functions remain supported for projects that use them, but package folders are not required by the language or its examples. Scripts are not excitation generators because they lack an argument/output contract and depend on mutable base-workspace and path state.

Initial conditions are model-owned reusable physical state and are selected by the consuming analysis; a reusable model never hard-codes a study step name. The closed kinds cover structural displacement, velocity, and angular velocity; thermal temperature; electric potential; magnetic vector potential; acoustic pressure; and fluid pressure and velocity. A condition has exactly one strongly typed source: a finite uniform scalar/vector, an exact non-frequency signal sample with a typed coordinate and explicit discontinuity side, or an immutable field artifact whose content, topology, field, quantity, shape, frame, and completeness are checked at admission. Vector state requires an explicit frame. The study-binding pass alone creates `applies_before_step` and its state input; compatible upstream state takes precedence unless the procedure declares a typed replacement policy, and conflicting state is rejected rather than combined implicitly. `check` performs schema, callable-resolution, static signature, effect, capability, unit, and policy validation without executing user code. `plan` constructs the materialization and solve graph without claiming generated values are valid. `run` executes the materialization task, validates and publishes its artifact, then admits dependent mesh/assembly/solve tasks. A separately exposed materialize operation may be added if evidence shows users need to inspect or approve generated inputs before a solve.

obligations.criterion: Modal eigenvalue extraction has no excitation. Forced use of modes is represented by separate procedures: modal transient response from time histories; modal harmonic response from complex frequency-domain excitations; modal response-spectrum analysis from a typed design or shock response spectrum; and random vibration response from PSD and cross-PSD inputs. Computing a shock response spectrum from a base-acceleration time history is a general signal-processing operation. Consuming that spectrum with structural modes is an FEA modal-response procedure. Do not call both operations `modal analysis` or treat an SRS as an unnamed frequency/value table. A typed response spectrum retains: natural frequency or period abscissa and units; damping ratio or quality factor; response ordinate quantity: relative displacement/velocity/acceleration, absolute acceleration, or an explicitly defined pseudo quantity; positive, negative, or maximax envelope convention; construction method and sampling adequacy evidence when derived from a history; interpolation and extrapolation policy; base direction and frame; spectrum and directional combination rules; modal truncation, participation, residual-mode, rigid-response, and missing-mass policy; and provenance and content digest. Modal-response results include participation factors, effective modal mass by direction, cumulative captured mass, per-mode response, correlation/combination evidence, missing-mass contribution where enabled, and the modes actually used. SRSS is accepted only under its documented separation assumptions. CQC or another explicitly supported correlation method is required where closely spaced modes invalidate those assumptions. Directional combination and modal combination are distinct policies.

obligations.criterion: Generated physical input has layered identity: Typed contract structure: generator provenance = program revision + callable identity + captures + declared frozen inputs signal realization = canonical samples/field + quantity + units + interpolation + error evidence solver excitation = signal realization + spatial projection + activation + procedure Study provenance includes the generator identity and realization digest. Numerical caches may reuse a realization with identical canonical content while preserving distinct authored provenance. Code changes, capture changes, sampling-policy changes, frozen-input changes, or materialized output changes invalidate the appropriate layer. Materialization uses the existing driver, program bundle, `ValuePayload`, object store, encryption, cancellation, retry, and publication fencing. The Server remains content-blind. A generated artifact is published once per logical identity and reused by sweep entries, load cases, and distributed ranks. Small signals may be broadcast. Large time histories and topology fields use manifest-plus-chunk artifacts, partial transfer, and partition-aware access. Every rank applies the same canonical interpolation contract. GPU-resident generation is allowed when ordinary RunMat placement supports it, but the published artifact still has provider-neutral identity and truthful transfer evidence. A callable does not become a GPU solver kernel merely because it was evaluated on a GPU.

obligations.criterion: Required governed cases include: constant, piecewise-linear, step, and complex frequency-dependent signals; discontinuities, domain boundaries, interpolation, extrapolation rejection, and adaptive materialization error; closure capture and named project function equivalence to an explicit table; source/capture changes invalidating identity and identical canonical realizations reusing numerical work correctly; rejection of mutable, nondeterministic, unavailable, or nonportable callable dependencies; inline, isolated-process, durable, and encrypted remote materialization equivalence; retry, cancellation, stale-publication fencing, and artifact reuse; static force/moment resultants and transient work/energy balance; prescribed displacement/velocity/acceleration consistency; base acceleration and modal participation factors; SRS construction references and modal response-spectrum SRSS/CQC, directional-combination, truncation, and missing-mass references; harmonic complex amplitude and phase; thermal, electrical, electromagnetic, acoustic, and fluid source/boundary histories; mesh-dependent spatial field projection and conservation; partition-independent distributed interpolation and source assembly; and explicit CPU/GPU transfer, precision, synchronization, and fallback evidence.

RunMat language and general numerical libraries; Generate, import, filter, resample, transform, and combine arrays using ordinary functions, closures, signal-processing operations, control-system models, data APIs, and accelerator execution.. `runmat-analysis-core`; Own strongly typed signals, physical quantities, excitations, initial conditions, response spectra, targets, frames, activation, and interpolation intent.. `runmat-analysis-fea`; Realize signals and spatial actions on canonical topology, form load/source vectors and boundary terms, compute modal participation and spectral combinations, and publish realization evidence.. obligations.criterion: An engineering study is an ordered semantic sequence of procedures, not merely one procedure plus an execution task graph. `runmat-analysis-core` owns the authored sequence. `runmat-analysis-fea` validates procedure compatibility, realizes state transitions, and records their evidence. The generic execution graph schedules that already validated sequence; it cannot invent physical dependencies or decide which state is meaningful to transfer. The public model contains: `AnalysisSequence`, with stable step identities and an explicit directed acyclic dependency graph; `ProcedureStep`, with one typed physics family, analysis procedure, solution space, activation set, output requests, accuracy policy, and formulation options; `StateInput`, naming the required upstream state kind and admissible source step; `StateOutput`, naming the state actually published by a completed step; `StateTransition`, defining compatibility, projection, linearization, and reference-state policy between two steps; and `SequenceBranch`, allowing multiple downstream procedures to consume the same immutable persisted state without rerunning or mutating the producer. The inter-step semantic graph is acyclic. Nonlinear iterations, contact active-set updates, partitioned coupling, and adaptive solve/estimate/refine cycles occur inside a governed procedure step and are represented by its checkpointed execution subgraph; they are not back-edges that obscure which completed physical state a later procedure consumes. Closed enums and family-specific types represent procedure and state kinds. Strings may name steps, regions, and authored objects, but do not select transition behavior. At minimum, state contracts distinguish: converged primary fields and their topology;

obligations.criterion: velocities, accelerations, and time-integrator state; temperature and thermal reference state; stress, strain, geometric-stiffness, and material-history state; contact active-set and friction history where the receiving procedure permits it; fluid state and moving-mesh/ALE state; electromagnetic complex or static field state; modal bases, normalization, participation, and truncation metadata; and coupled-interface state and relaxation history.

Loads, sources, constraints, contacts, interfaces, initial conditions, output requests, and supported material parameters declare step-scoped activation. Activation is a typed lifecycle of `Activate`, `Continue`, `Modify`, or `Deactivate`; absence is not interpreted as an implicit continuation. A modification produces a new authored identity while retaining attribution to the original object. Every step declares its own independent variable and origin. Total study time, step-local time, frequency, eigenvalue parameter, load factor, and iteration count are distinct typed domains. A transition must explicitly map any continuing schedule into the receiving domain. Restarting a transient step does not reset physical time unless the authored sequence says so. Initial conditions apply only where no compatible upstream state supplies the same quantity, unless a typed override policy explicitly replaces or augments that state. Conflicts are rejected before execution.

Initial production transitions include: static structural state to prestressed modal extraction; static or supported nonlinear structural state to eigenvalue buckling; static or supported nonlinear structural state to prestressed direct or modal harmonic response; thermal state to structural temperature, thermal strain, and prestress; completed transient state to a continuation or restart of the same formulation; modal extraction state to modal transient, harmonic, response-spectrum, or random response; converged family states into the supported coupled procedures; and parent-mesh state to an adapted mesh through the separately governed adaptation transfer. Each transition declares whether it reuses a field, projects it, linearizes about it, derives a new operator contribution, or uses it only as an initial guess. These meanings are never conflated. In particular: procedure-specific physics and numerical settings use a closed typed canonical union rather than string maps or runtime defaults. Random response, for example, authors modal damping and the required cumulative modal-mass ratio on the procedure; task interval grouping and iteration ceilings remain placement-neutral numerical execution policy; prestressed procedures consume a converged base state and derive the documented tangent and geometric-stiffness contributions; an initial guess does not become a physical initial condition; a visualization interpolation is never accepted as solver state transfer; stateful plasticity or contact history is transferred only when the receiving formulation and mesh-transfer evidence support it; and unsupported topology, units, frames, formulations, or state revisions fail with an attributable transition diagnostic.

obligations.criterion: Every state-producing step publishes an immutable, typed state manifest before dependent steps are admitted. The manifest includes producer-step identity, topology and partition identities, physical time or load parameter, field and history digests, reference conventions, linearization point, constraint plan, precision, and completeness evidence. A restart resumes an interrupted procedure from a collectively valid checkpoint. A branch begins a new procedure from a completed immutable state. A retry repeats an execution attempt for the same logical step. These are different operations and have different identities. No checkpoint or partial field may be relabeled as a completed base state. Downstream logical identity includes the complete semantic transition and upstream state digest. Placement, worker count, attempt, and physical chunk boundaries remain execution evidence. Independent downstream branches may run concurrently and reuse the same state artifact. A tightly coupled or stateful step retains the group-level checkpoint and epoch rules required for cooperative execution.

requirements.title: Semantic procedure transitions and immutable completed state

obligations.criterion: Results are requested through a typed observation system. It prevents accidental production of enormous result sets, supports useful answers without full-field transfer, and keeps result selection separate from visualization. Calling `plot` or `mesh` never decides what physical quantity to recover. The authored output contract distinguishes: `FieldOutput`: a spatial field snapshot or governed series over a typed region and topology location; `HistoryOutput`: relatively frequent values for a bounded point, entity set, connector, reference point, interface, or global quantity; `ProbeOutput`: a point evaluation or spatial aggregate intended for inspection or monitoring; `ReductionOutput`: an integral, average, norm, resultant, moment, minimum, maximum, RMS, variance, envelope, or another explicitly supported typed reduction; `DiagnosticOutput`: convergence, balance, constraint, contact, adaptation, and resource evidence; and `Monitor`: a bounded scalar observation evaluated during solution for progress or a typed termination criterion. Every request declares: a stable request identity and producing procedure step; physical quantity and value shape; target region, entity, reference point, connector, interface, or whole-model scope; source location such as nodal, cell, element, integration point, face, edge, modal, or global; requested output location and the governed recovery or interpolation required to obtain it; component, invariant, coordinate frame, sign convention, and complex representation where applicable; sampling domain and schedule: final, every accepted increment, named points, interval, event, frequency set, mode set, or adaptive policy; spatial and series reduction policies, including tie behavior for extrema;

tests.boundary: Tet4/Tet10 sampled topology retains original four/fifteen-point rule identities, positions, edge IDs and integration indices and rejects mismatched topology/count; no recovered-value convergence or global distributed reduction.
tests.name: results::observation::topology::tests::sampled_observation_topology_retains_each_original_rule_order_and_identity

obligations.criterion: precision, compression, retention, and partial-access policy; whether it is required for solver control, publication, visualization, or downstream sequence state; and an estimate of computation, resident memory, stored bytes, transfer, and collective cost. Quantity and reduction compatibility is validated before solve. A tensor invariant is not a string expression, a complex field cannot silently lose phase, an integration-point value cannot be called nodal without a recovery policy, and an extreme value must retain its value, location, producing step, sample coordinate, and tie policy.

Field recovery belongs to the producing physics family. Observation evaluation consumes those governed fields or explicitly documented solver-available quantities. It may compose typed operations but cannot recreate family equations or reach into private solver storage. Derived quantities use a typed expression or operation graph over admitted physical quantities. It checks dimensions, shapes, topology locations, frames, real/complex domains, and differentiability metadata. Ordinary RunMat functions may construct output data or post-process a published result, but no live language callback executes inside element recovery, a distributed reduction, or a solver monitor. Reusable generated post-processing follows the same freezing and materialization principles as generated excitations. Output expressions do not create a second FEA builtin namespace. Extend the canonical RunMat builtin/operation catalog with typed overloads and frontend applicability. One public operation identity such as `max` may have an ordinary numeric-tensor runtime binding and FEA field, history, or sweep-case lowerings. The FEA compiler selects an overload statically and lowers it to a canonical observation plan; the runtime binding remains runtime-owned. Domain-specific operations such as `resultant` and surface `moment` register in that same catalog and may expose compatible `.m` object overloads. Do not add an untracked parser keyword list, analysis-private name table, or separate documentation registry.

Each overload declares typed inputs/named arguments/output, quantity and unit transformation, shape, scalar/complex/statistical domain, field location/frame/coordinate rules, purity and effects, distributability, reduction ordering and tie policy, equivalence, cost shape, frontend availability, lowering owner, and documentation. The catalog drives parser/LSP completion, hover, signature help, named-argument completion, diagnostics, and generated reference material. Spatial/series/case extrema return typed attributed extrema rather than bare numbers. The value retains its physical quantity; the result also carries canonical entity/location or independent coordinate/case, source, and tie/reduction evidence. Vector/tensor/complex/statistical values need an explicit valid projection or representation before scalar extrema. Therefore the target syntax uses `max`, not a divergent `maximum`, and exposes `.value` or `.location` only where the inferred extremum type supports them. Default output sets are procedure-specific, small, documented, and versioned. Explicit requests replace or extend defaults according to a typed policy; omission never means “store every supported variable.” Requests that affect recovery, solver state retention, checkpoint content, or computation participate in the appropriate logical identity. The runtime-facing separation remains: `fea.field` and `fea.probe` select or evaluate analysis results. Ordinary `plot` and `mesh` render compatible values and remain compatible with their non-FEA MATLAB behavior.

requirements.title: Typed field recovery, bounded observations and monitors

tests.boundary: Two executions of one random-response study from a script keep one definition run id, publish distinct attempts, and the definition id resolves to the latest attempt. Remote placement and retry attempts inside one execution are not exercised.

obligations.criterion: A canonical logical study identity includes: geometry source identity and admitted geometry revision; canonical mesh request or solver-mesh digest; authored problem and material assignments; authored signal, excitation, initial-condition, response-spectrum, and combination contracts; generator provenance for generated authored inputs; materialized signal/field digests enter the downstream realized-study and solver-excitation identities after materialization; semantic analysis sequence, step identities, activation lifecycle, state-transition policies, and upstream state digests; physics family and analysis procedure for every step; formulation and numerical tolerances that can affect the mathematical result; typed observation requests when they affect recovery, retained solver state, computation, or canonical publication; requested accuracy and acceptance policy; and deterministic/numerical backend policy where it can affect accepted result equivalence. It excludes: local, durable, or remote placement; cluster and queue; worker count and partition layout; retry attempts; temporary paths; physical artifact locations; UI session IDs; and attach or detach behavior.

The shared CLI placement surface should preserve local defaults and reuse current cluster vocabulary: The reusable placement options are: project selection; cluster selection; queue, defaulting consistently with `job submit`; worker count, with zero retaining its existing driver-only/automatic meaning; trust identity, preferably supplied by project or named target configuration; idempotency key; attach/detach behavior; and machine-readable output. Do not require users to wrap `.fea` or meshing requests in a synthetic MATLAB script. `job submit` remains the generic MATLAB-program entrypoint. `runmat run file.fea` and `runmat mesh` prepare domain-specific encrypted execution bundles and reuse the lower-level submission lifecycle. An authored execution-policy reference is optional. Its absence means the CLI/project defaults choose placement, backend, and resources; it does not make the study incomplete. If present, the policy may express placement preference, elastic resource bounds, independent fanout, cooperative-distribution requirements, accelerator preference, and resilience. It cannot change physics or accuracy. CLI placement overrides use the same typed policy merge and may choose an equivalent location or tighten bounds without changing study-definition identity.

Execute one complete study on one allocated worker. Materialize and validate callable-backed signals before admitting dependent assembly or solve work. Preserve the existing local inline behavior as the default. Support local process isolation, durable local execution, and remote execution. Publish the same logical result and evidence shape across placements.

tests.boundary: A two-frequency native fan-out and fan-in publishes samples in authored order with recovered fields per frequency; order independence under reversed completion is in the sibling response-spectrum test.
tests.name: analysis_kernel::frequency_tests::native_frequency_fanout_and_fanin_are_portable_and_order_independent

obligations.criterion: Execute independent sweep entries concurrently. Deduplicate shared geometry, mesh, signal, response-spectrum, and realized-excitation artifacts by logical digest. Permit independent frequency points, load cases, parameter samples, sequence branches, observation reductions, and study variants to become tasks when their result composition is deterministic. Honor fail-fast and collect-all policies without losing already completed evidence.

Partition element or cell assembly. Use deterministic sparse contribution composition. Add distributed matrix-vector and preconditioner strategies only after the serial operator is verified. Define capability requirements by formulation, order, scalar type, backend, and required native kernel. Establish strong and appropriately tolerance-bounded result equivalence against the serial reference.

Represent sequence progression, coupled iterations, and adaptive iterations as checkpointed graph progression. Fence iteration publication so stale attempts cannot commit state. Transfer only canonical field/history artifacts between stages. Make convergence decisions deterministic from persisted evidence.

Use driver-owned scheduling already supported by worker allocations. Do not create nested independent schedulers inside FEA solvers. An analysis root job owns a task graph containing only the granularity justified for its level. Initially this is frozen-input admission, any required signal materialization, a mesh prerequisite, excitation realization, validated procedure-step execution, observation evaluation, and result publication. Data-independent materialization and meshing may run concurrently. Independent sequence branches may run concurrently after their immutable producer state is published. Verified solvers can later expand assembly, linear algebra, coupling, adaptation, or distributed reductions into child tasks. The semantic sequence is compiled into the task graph; it is not reconstructed from task edges. Execution retries, repartitioning, or placement changes cannot alter step activation, state meaning, or transition policy. Meshing invoked by a study remains the same canonical meshing graph used by standalone `runmat mesh`; analysis consumes its artifact rather than reimplementing meshing stages.

Independent distribution uses the existing durable task model for whole studies, mesh stages, sweep entries, load cases, frequency points, recovery partitions, and other replay-safe tasks. These tasks communicate through immutable content-addressed artifacts and may be retried independently under the existing effect policy. Cooperative distributed algebra is a different execution class. It requires: gang allocation of a compatible worker group; a stable group and partition epoch; deterministic partition-to-worker ownership; peer routing and authenticated channels; halo exchange and collective reduction contracts; iteration barriers and collective cancellation; topology- and accelerator-aware resource admission; coordinated checkpoint and restart; and group-level failure semantics. The existing driver remains the sole scheduler. The FEA solver supplies a numerical partition/communication plan and participates through the existing `GangHandle`/`SpmdTaskContext` generation and collective identities; it does not start a nested scheduler. The generic execution and runner crates own gang and collective lifecycle semantics, while `runmat-execution-runner-native` implements the native and encrypted remote transport behavior. Language-level `ValuePayload` collectives are the functional baseline, not automatically the high-throughput numerical data plane. Benchmark reduction latency, payload copying, coordinator pressure, halo throughput, and device-resident behavior. Any required bulk extension retains the same gang generation, rank, collective sequence, cancellation, causal failure, authentication, and fencing contracts.

tests.boundary: A remote rank failure releases a peer blocked in a collective within five seconds and surfaces the primary structured error with its source ordinal; SPMD runtime program, not a numerical solve.

obligations.criterion: A failed independent task may retry alone. A lost participant in a tightly coupled Krylov, nonlinear, or coupled iteration cannot publish or retry independently. The group either recovers from a collectively valid checkpoint or restarts under a new epoch. Stale epochs are fenced from all state and result publication.

The partition plan defines owned and ghost DOFs, elements/cells, constraint rows, interfaces, and result ranges. It has its own execution identity and evidence but does not alter authored-problem or discretized-problem identity. No worker independently guesses ownership. Distributed assembly emits partition-local canonical contributions. A global matrix is not gathered unless a selected small-problem backend explicitly requires it. Distributed operator application declares halo messages and collective reductions, and preconditioners declare their communication topology and setup/reuse lifetime. Multi-GPU execution is the composition of accelerator-local kernels with cooperative distributed algebra. It is not implied by requesting several GPU workers and is not advertised until halo transfer, collective reduction, failure, and numerical evidence pass.

obligations.criterion: Parallel element/cell assembly into partition-local contribution buffers. Deterministic merge ordering for reproducible modes. Parallel recovery and balance evaluation. Bounded memory and cancellation checkpoints.

Partition by canonical element/cell identities. Externalize immutable partition inputs. Produce canonical contribution artifacts with exact ownership. Join contributions deterministically and reject duplicates or omissions.

obligations.criterion: Begin with embarrassingly parallel studies, load cases, and frequencies. Add distributed sparse matrix-vector work and preconditioning family by family. Define halo/ghost ownership, communication budgets, convergence aggregation, and failure recovery explicitly. Never claim bitwise equivalence when floating-point reduction order makes only tolerance-bounded equivalence meaningful; encode the applicable equivalence policy in evidence. Compare local inline, isolated process, durable, and remote results against the same verified serial reference.

Capabilities should describe actual worker requirements, including: analysis host ABI; physics formulation and implementation revision; element order and supported topology; scalar/complex precision; CPU instruction or accelerator class where required; deterministic platform cohort where strict replay requires it; native exact-CAD kernel only for tasks that perform geometry admission or meshing; and memory, scratch, wall-time, artifact, egress, and relay budgets.

Re-audit current `origin/dev`; consume landed typed value, gang, collective, distributed, accelerator, and provider contracts before adding any platform-facing type. Reuse the already-public `runmat-types` numeric and storage facts immediately where their semantics are exact; do not wait for the broader runtime migration to duplicate them locally. Define canonical study, sequence, step, state-transition, workload, task, observation, accuracy, result, and publication identities in `runmat-analysis-fea`, including layered generator, signal-realization, and solver-excitation identities. Define analysis worker capabilities and artifact media/schema contracts. Include canonical constraint-plan inputs, identities, evidence, and publication ownership in analysis tasks. Define the layered problem, discretization, operator, numerical-plan, execution-plan, attempt, and result identities. Add the analysis workload executable form and typed host ABI through the generic artifact and runner contracts. Define manifest-plus-chunk numerical objects for mesh, signal, response spectrum, realized excitation, field, semantic state, history, observation, accuracy evidence, operator, and checkpoint data. Implement the native analysis provider alongside the existing meshing provider. Split meshing stage execution into one immutable bundle-authorized host program and a run-scoped, externalized invocation descriptor. Dynamically planned stages must reuse the same program artifact; the descriptor and its declared semantic roots are validated together before a kernel runs.

Make the existing meshing-owned exact DAG orchestration awaitable and implement a remote pool executor over the generic runner. Keep the driver as the root-workload orchestrator and workers as stage kernels; do not duplicate the DAG, wrap CAD in MATLAB, or create nested worker-side scheduling. Add a portable exact-meshing root workload with chunked source-CAD admission and a canonical terminal mesh/evidence closure. Remote CAD admission must not require a local OCCT installation, and actual run authority and platform evidence must never be accepted from the payload. Add shared placement arguments to `runmat run` and `runmat mesh` only as their corresponding execution shapes become real. Central validation must reject unsupported combinations before compilation, CAD import, path reservation, or network work. Support whole-study local-process, durable, and remote execution. Compile validated semantic sequences into execution graphs; execute independent sweep entries and immutable sequence branches concurrently and remotely through the same graph. Resolve named `.fea` project callables and language closures through the existing callable and frozen-project machinery; add typed static signature, effect, capability, capture, and portability admission. Implement bounded callable materialization tasks that publish canonical signal or mesh-dependent field artifacts before dependent work, without live solver callbacks. Deduplicate shared geometry, mesh, signal, spectrum, and excitation artifacts. Add progress, cancellation, retry, attach, recovery, and fenced-publication conformance, including materialization tasks.

Add Desktop placement and lifecycle integration using generic execution services and partial result access, including sequence/step state, generated physical inputs, observations, accuracy status, and provenance. Add conformance tests for borrowed, moved, materialized, device-resident, and distributed value admission, including copy-accounting and forbidden implicit-conversion cases. A simple verified study and a standalone mesh produce equivalent logical outputs in inline, isolated-process, durable, and remote shapes. A sweep demonstrates bounded parallel execution and deterministic composition. Explicit tables and equivalent callable-generated inputs produce equivalent canonical realizations in inline, isolated-process, durable, and encrypted remote execution. Callable source, capture, frozen-input, sampling-policy, and realized-content changes invalidate the correct identity layer; retries cannot publish stale generated input. Large inputs and results travel as closed, chunked artifacts rather than inline values or driver-gathered payloads. The Server remains content-blind. Placement is absent from logical study identity. Constraint identity and results are independent of worker count and partition layout. Semantic step ordering, activation, state transitions, and branch results are independent of execution scheduling and retries. Bounded histories and partial observations can be queried without gathering unrelated full fields.

requirements.title: Placement-independent logical studies and governed scheduling

obligations.criterion: The analysis system owns the mathematical operator; RunMat's generic compute substrate owns execution representations and placement. This boundary must be explicit before production families proliferate.

tests.boundary: Sparse reduction matches dense lifting and preserves operator properties.
tests.name: constraints::algebra::tests::sparse_reduction_matches_dense_lifting_and_preserves_operator_properties

obligations.criterion: Every assembled or matrix-free operator declares: scalar domain and precision; dimensions and block structure; symmetry or Hermitian status; positive-definite, semidefinite, indefinite, or unknown classification; null-space and gauge information; sparse pattern identity and numeric-value revision when assembled; constraint-plan identity; partition plan when distributed; apply, transpose-apply, and adjoint-apply support as applicable; and memory, scratch, and communication estimates. The sparse pattern and its numeric values have separate identities. Geometry, topology, or constraint-structure changes invalidate the pattern. Material, frequency, load-step, or state changes invalidate numeric values only when they actually affect them. Multiple load cases may reuse an operator; nonlinear iterations may reuse a pattern while replacing values. Assembly produces deterministic, canonical contribution records and composes them into one shared sparse representation. Structural, thermal, electromagnetic, acoustic, and fluid families must not create private CSR variants or separate sparse merge rules.

Three sparse representations remain deliberately distinct: MATLAB-facing sparse values, which implement language-visible value semantics; portable execution sparse values and chunked numerical artifacts, which implement transport and persistence; and the canonical analysis operator, which implements numerical semantics and efficient application. Conversions are explicit, validated adapters. `runmat-analysis-fea` does not depend on `runmat-value`, and a live solver operator is never defined by runtime `Value` or MATLAB storage behavior. Transport encodings may use CSC while an operator uses CSR or block CSR; that is not duplication when each has one documented owner. The adapter contract is typed on both sides. Its runtime side accepts `ValueFact` plus borrowed or owned `runmat-value` storage; its analysis side accepts the canonical analysis scalar class, dimensions, layout, index width, and ownership mode. Admission either proves a zero-copy borrow/move, performs and records a conversion, or returns a typed incompatibility. It never silently narrows precision, drops a complex component, changes index width, gathers a distributed value, or transfers between host and device.

Physics assembly returns a `DiscreteOperator`, not a CPU, GPU, or distributed solver object. A typed `LinearSolvePlan` then selects a compatible algorithm, preconditioner, tolerance policy, precision policy, and restart policy. Preparation produces one of: a host prepared operator; an accelerator-provider-owned prepared operator; or a distributed prepared operator over an explicit partition and worker-group epoch. Backend modules implement the same operator and solve contracts. They do not duplicate formulation logic, constraint semantics, convergence policy, or result recovery.

obligations.criterion: Extend `runmat-accelerate-api` with provider-neutral sparse descriptors, opaque sparse handles, capabilities, feasibility queries, and costs. Do not put WGPU objects or `GpuTensorHandle` values into the canonical analysis operator. The accelerator provider owns device buffers and exposes only capability-checked operations. Native CUDA sparse libraries and WGPU implementations may sit behind that same operation contract. Provider-owned native device context and buffer export can avoid redundant copies, but it is an implementation seam rather than a second FEA accelerator API. FEA must not directly own CUDA contexts, streams, allocation, or WGPU devices. The initial sparse operation surface includes: pattern and numeric-value upload with separate reuse lifetimes; real and complex CSR matrix-vector and matrix-multivector products; dot products, norms, reductions, and fused Krylov vector updates; sparse triangular application when natively supported; preconditioner setup and application; supported index widths, block forms, scalar types, and transpose/adjoint modes; allocation, scratch, cancellation, concurrency, and transactional-result behavior; and truthful operation-level timing, transfer, synchronization, and fallback evidence. Provider defaults return unsupported. They never download, execute on the host, and re-upload while reporting successful GPU execution. Fallback may occur only through the shared placement decision before result commitment and must record the reason and the operations that actually ran.

GPU capability is promoted by operation and solver envelope, not as one boolean claim: resident vector operations and reductions; native sparse matrix-vector application; a complete real-SPD Krylov path; a useful production preconditioner path; complex sparse operations and compatible Krylov methods; nonsymmetric, indefinite, and block systems; accelerator assembly and recovery where measurements justify them; and multi-accelerator execution only after single-worker GPU execution is mature. Each promoted envelope governs precision, maximum host synchronizations, transfer bytes, device-resident work ratio, setup cost, iteration time, memory use, convergence, and CPU-reference equivalence. Moving completed arrays to a device or running only vector updates there is not a GPU solve.

tests.name: solve::linear::tests::scoped_pcg_matches_serial_and_rejects_nested_execution

obligations.criterion: Local parallelism uses execution-resource-aware, scoped pools. It must not depend on an unconstrained global thread pool or oversubscribe CPUs through nested sweep, assembly, BLAS, solver, and provider concurrency. Plans account for memory bandwidth, bounded contribution buffers, accelerator queues, and NUMA where material. Deterministic mode fixes contribution and reduction order; throughput mode may use tolerance-governed reductions and records that policy.

obligations.criterion: Use distinct canonical identities for: authored problem; semantic analysis sequence and procedure step; upstream state and state transition; discretized problem and solver mesh; constraint plan; operator structure; operator numeric values; numerical solve plan; observation and accuracy plan; execution and partition plan; attempt and worker-group epoch; and published result and evidence. CPU and GPU may realize the same numerical solve plan. Worker count, partition layout, placement, queue, and retry never change the authored or discretized identities, but they are mandatory execution evidence. Solver tolerances and algorithms belong to numerical-plan identity. Provider/device identity belongs to execution evidence unless the authored policy explicitly requests a provider-specific numerical envelope.

Do not duplicate its domain-specific types. Meshes, operator patterns and values, partition maps, fields, semantic states, histories, observations, accuracy evidence, preconditioner checkpoints, and solver checkpoints use manifest-plus-chunk objects with: a logical digest independent of physical chunk boundaries; typed media and schema contracts; bounded chunk and total sizes; partial and partition-local access; complete closure validation; resumable verified transfer; ownership and lineage evidence; and explicit retention and reuse policy. Large matrices and result fields are never passed as ordinary inline task values or forced through the driver. Full-resolution results remain canonical artifacts; plotting and Desktop consume partial fields or separately identified visualization products without replacing the canonical numerical result.

obligations.criterion: Geometric recovery, location and local topology queries declare their search work and retained state. Repeated local queries use maintained incidence, local traversal or conservative spatial candidates instead of repeatedly scanning the full inventory when locality permits it. Candidate pruning preserves exact predicates, degeneracy handling, deterministic ordering and topology validity. Index construction, mutation, rollback and cycle history remain accounted and cancellable. If a global traversal is necessary, its necessity, frequency and cost are explicit and evidenced; no search-budget exemption is implied. A bounded scheduling window cannot starve other unresolved sources or be treated as exhaustive failure. Cooperative size/shape convergence retains its accepted working state and valid indexes; unavoidable complete handoffs have explicit triggers and measured frequency. Rejection reuse binds the full local topology, metric and protected-boundary dependencies or invalidates conservatively. Useful accepted progress, rejected-candidate work and complete-state reconstructions are measured together. Synthetic scheduling priorities verify scheduling only, not physical convergence. Automatic geometric sizing retains the measured physical directions of curvature, feature and gap constraints. Repeated samples cannot invent additional density in unrelated directions. obligations.criterion: A converged algebraic solve is not automatically an accurate engineering result. Every procedure step therefore owns a typed `AccuracyPlan` and publishes an `AccuracyReport`. These coordinate existing family-specific controls without pretending that unlike error measures can always be collapsed into one rigorous scalar bound. An authored accuracy plan may declare: target quantities or observations whose accuracy matters; absolute and relative tolerances with physical dimensions where applicable; required estimator, convergence-study, balance, or residual evidence; maximum admissible spatial, temporal, frequency, coupling, modal-truncation, stochastic, transfer, interpolation, recovery, and algebraic contributions; deterministic or tolerance-bounded execution equivalence; action when evidence is unavailable or a limit is exceeded: refine, tighten, extend, warn under an explicitly non-production policy, or fail; and resource ceilings that bound automatic refinement or solver tightening. The resulting report attributes, where applicable: geometry-admission and boundary-approximation evidence; mesh quality and spatial discretization estimates; linear residual and conditioning evidence; nonlinear residual, increment, complementarity, and load-step evidence; time-integration or frequency-sampling evidence; modal residual, basis truncation, correlation, residual-mode, and missing-mass evidence; stochastic sampling or spectral-integration evidence; interface projection, field transfer, and coupled-iteration closure; observation recovery, interpolation, sampling, and reduction evidence; and precision, reduction-order, backend, and placement-equivalence evidence.

obligations.criterion: Each contribution retains its own norm, units, estimator assumptions, scope, and provenance. The system does not add dimensionally or statistically incompatible values into a decorative “total error.” It instead evaluates a typed acceptance predicate, identifies the governing unmet criterion, and distinguishes: `Satisfied`: every mandatory criterion has passing evidence; `NotSatisfied`: at least one mandatory criterion failed; `Indeterminate`: required evidence is unavailable or does not bound the requested quantity; and `NotApplicable`: a contribution is provably irrelevant to this procedure. Publication requires `Satisfied`, or `Indeterminate` under an explicit markIndeterminate policy with visible evidence. `Indeterminate` cannot silently pass because the solver residual is small, and `NotSatisfied` always blocks publication. Accuracy planning is staged. Before meshing it can choose a formulation, order, initial mesh policy, time/frequency sampling, modal range, and solver class. After topology projection it updates resource and error estimates. During solve it may perform bounded, checkpointed refinement or tolerance changes when the authored policy permits them. It may never relax a requested criterion to fit resources. If the goal is infeasible under the resource ceiling, planning or execution returns an attributable failure.

Target-quantity accuracy integrates with typed observations. A target must be computable on the current formulation and carry a valid recovery and sampling policy. Adaptive analysis consumes the same accuracy plan rather than defining a parallel convergence authority. Coupled studies retain both per-family contributions and interface/global closure; one passing component cannot hide another failing component. Accuracy identity includes target quantities, tolerances, estimators, refinement/tightening actions, stopping policy, and any numerical choices capable of changing the accepted result. Placement and worker layout remain evidence unless the authored numerical-equivalence policy makes them mathematically relevant. Required governed cases include: a tight algebraic solve on an under-resolved mesh being rejected or refined rather than accepted; spatial refinement reducing a validated estimator and target-quantity change at the expected rate; time-step, frequency-grid, modal-basis, and coupling tolerances independently governing acceptance; interpolation or transfer error blocking an otherwise converged coupled result; `Indeterminate` when a requested quantity lacks a valid estimator or convergence study; bounded automatic refinement respecting cancellation, checkpoint, retry, and resource ceilings; and equivalent acceptance decisions across inline, remote, partitioned, CPU, and claimed GPU execution.

requirements.title: Typed numerical accuracy acceptance and bounded refinement

obligations.criterion: The completion scope does not include general optimization, inverse analysis, uncertainty quantification, topology optimization, arbitrary user elements, or arbitrary executable constitutive laws. The architecture must nevertheless avoid closing off two valuable RunMat integrations. First, authored models and observations retain a typed parameter-dependency graph. A future design-study layer can identify bounded design variables, uncertain inputs, response functions, objectives, and design constraints without parsing strings or inspecting solver internals. Each operator, state transition, and observation may declare derivative support as an enum such as analytic tangent, automatic differentiation compatible, governed numerical difference, or unavailable. This is capability metadata, not a claim that gradients or optimization are implemented. Ordinary sweeps and independent parameter samples remain in the present production scope and reuse the existing task, artifact, cache, and cluster infrastructure. Second, state-dependent executable laws retain the separate compiled-law boundary described above. Their future ABI must make typed state, outputs, consistent derivatives, purity/effects, checkpointing, CPU/GPU/distributed capability, and verification explicit. Neither future seam permits a live RunMat callback inside assembly, recovery, an iterative solve, or a distributed rank.

requirements.title: Truthful future derivative and compiled-law seams

Separate the admitted formulation from numerical quality and publication status. Centralize pre-assembly formulation admission. Resolve the typed family, procedure, solution space, model, and mesh through one registry into an opaque admitted formulation receipt. Only that receipt may construct persisted run identity; callers cannot manufacture or mutate an identity. Record the exact realization that executed, including spatial element/operator formulation, temporal integration, constitutive update, coupling transfer, field recovery, topology source, source projection, and boundary projection. Distinguish Tet4, Tet10, beam, shell, synthetic structural operators, inferred lattices, generated graphs, reduced channels, adjacency recovery, and resampled/profile transfers rather than hiding them behind broad family labels. Add typed admission failures for unregistered formulations, noncanonical topology or projection, malformed/unsupported connectivity, unsupported mixed-dimensional assembly, unmapped sources, missing interfaces, incompatible procedures, and unqualified recovery or transfer. Reject before solver progress or artifact publication.

Add typed analysis-sequence, procedure-step, state-input/output, transition, activation, branch, and restart contracts; keep them distinct from execution tasks. obligations.criterion: Implement and test the shared analysis projection. Implement one canonical property compiler from authored, geometry-resolved material/composite, section, layup, and orientation intent to an element-complete compiled property map. Bind its semantic digest to geometry revision and topology, keep audit evidence separate, and expose role/capability-specific immutable views rather than family-private lookup inventories. Implement typed constraint-target resolution and canonical constraint-plan compilation. Implement shared signal interpolation, breakpoint/extrapolation rules, derivative-consistent kinematics, spatial excitation realization, projection/conservation evidence, and family admissibility validation. Implement shared sparse constraint rows, affine reduction, multiplier, null-space, rank, and reaction mappings. Replace family-private matrix representations with the canonical sparse pattern, values, contribution, and operator contracts. Add typed operator properties and solver/preconditioner compatibility validation. Extend the generic accelerator API with sparse descriptors, opaque handles, feasibility, operations, and costs; unsupported remains the default. Implement and verify the serial CPU reference backend before any accelerator or distributed promotion. Implement shared observation target resolution, sampling, typed derived-operation validation, partition-local reduction, bounded history, and canonical publication contracts. Implement the study-level accuracy plan, contribution evidence, acceptance states, and family extension hooks without creating a second adaptive-convergence authority. Add post-projection numerical/resource planning and early admission or repartition decisions, including observation and bounded-accuracy work.

Move flow topology from runtime into analysis. Move acoustic, CFD, CHT, and FSI kernels out of runtime. Split runtime operations, documents, persistence, presentation, and policy. Split FEA topology, algebra, constraints, excitation, physics, orchestration, execution, results, and diagnostics. Add architecture tests for dependency direction, prohibited physics ownership in runtime, and prohibited runtime callable/value dependencies in analysis solvers. Remove superseded modules and duplicate rules, including family-private property lookup, coefficient averaging, schedule, and time-profile implementations. All geometry-dependent families consume the same projection. Runtime contains no element, cell, flux, constitutive, or coupling kernels. Region and boundary resolution has one implementation. Property selection and coverage have one compiler. Every active material-bearing element has one compatible homogeneous or composite constitutive owner plus every required section and orientation; gaps, overlaps, stale/empty scopes, wrong roles, missing capabilities, and geometry/topology substitution fail before assembly. No promoted operator, recovery path, coupling, or diagnostic derives constitutive coefficients from declaration order, global material averages, implicit defaults, importer confidence, or a family-private region matcher. Compiled property semantics and coefficients are invariant under authored ordering, partitioning, serialization, and supported execution placement. Constraint kinds, DOFs, frames, pairing, and enforcement are typed through the solver boundary. Signals, excitation targets, quantities, units, interpolation, activation, and spatial realization are typed through the solver boundary, with no live callback or duplicated family schedule authority.

Empty, conflicting, redundant, overconstrained, and underconstrained plans produce attributable diagnostics. Every promoted solver consumes the same canonical operator contract and rejects algebraically incompatible algorithms. Runtime sparse values, execution sparse values, and analysis operators have explicit one-way adapters and no ownership leakage. Field recovery, observation evaluation, plotting, and accuracy acceptance have distinct owners and no duplicated quantity/reduction logic. Distributed observations use partition ownership and governed collectives rather than driver-side full-field gathering. Resource estimates are checked against actual allocations before assembly begins. Structural preflight distinguishes topology-only stiffness upper bounds from the exact prepared operator: exhaustion of a bounded coercivity proof on the upper-bound pattern is indeterminate, not proof that the prepared operator is inadmissible. A supported envelope needs separately justified early admission and exact-operator solve evidence; neither a false-negative symbolic gate nor a silent post-assembly failure satisfies this gate. Module size and dependency checks prevent the known god-file structure from returning.

obligations.criterion: The supported surface comprises Tet4/Tet10 linear solids, three-dimensional beams, membrane/bending shells and deliberate mixed assembly; eigenmodes and prestressed modes; modal transient/harmonic, response-spectrum correlation/missing-mass and random PSD/cross-PSD response; eigenvalue buckling and prestressed direct/modal harmonic response from compatible converged state; direct transient/harmonic dynamics; geometric nonlinearity, supported plastic laws and frictionless/frictional contact; steady/transient conduction with supported sources and radiation; electrostatics, conduction, magnetostatics, harmonic multi-frequency and transient Maxwell and saturating magnetics; harmonic, modal and transient acoustics with impedance, radiation, transmission loss, intensity and structure-borne sound; steady/transient incompressible laminar flow with generalized-Newtonian, viscoelastic, porous, species, free-surface, rotating-frame, lubrication, electrokinetic, particle, low-Mach, compressible laminar and network physics; thermoelastic, electrothermal, conjugate heat transfer and two-way FSI; adaptation with validated family estimators and transfer. Every formulation runs through one thread plan, remotely and with domain decomposition, and independently satisfies all shared and family acceptance. No unsupported combination silently selects a reduced model.

Turbulence (RANS, LES, DES), perfectly matched layers, boundary elements, acoustic mean flow, antennas, waveguide ports, motors, piezoelectricity, fracture, fatigue, hexahedral, wedge and pyramid elements, view-factor radiation and arbitrary material models are outside the supported surface. They are rejected with typed diagnostics and the site makes no claim about them. Advertising any of them requires a new requirement with its own envelope and independent qualification; a future extension seam grants no implemented capability.

Each family follows authored-contract validation, frozen generated-input materialization, canonical mesh projection, typed property/constraint/source compilation, physical discretization and assembly, compatible numerical solution, physical field recovery, typed observation evaluation, accuracy evidence, governed publication and persistence. No stage has duplicate authoritative implementations or reaches backward into private host/syntax structures.

Converge the public platform baseline first and establish truthful contracts before parallel nonoverlapping work. Shared topology and algebra precede physical families. Linear structures plus semantic state transitions precede base-state linearization, buckling and prestressed modal/harmonic work. Constituent solvers meet their own gates before thermoelastic, electrothermal, conjugate heat transfer or FSI qualification. FSI additionally requires structural dynamics. Observations and shared accuracy acceptance precede final family promotion. Each adaptive family requires its validated estimator and state transfer. Duplicate ownership blocks family promotion even when numerical work begins behind stable interfaces.

Canonical topology and constraints precede canonical sparse operators/patterns, a verified serial CPU reference, resource-aware shared-memory execution, whole-study remote/independent task distribution, qualified single-accelerator sparse execution, cooperative worker-group/collective contracts, family-specific distributed algebra and justified multi-accelerator promotion. Scaling contracts arrive early; partitioned numerical work starts only after a correct serial operator. Fanout, host fallback, data transfers and metadata alone establish none of the downstream numerical gates.

Implementation work stays in the analysis checkout and uses the private platform checkout only for required Desktop/Server integration. The separately owned active general RunMat checkout must not be read, modified, built, formatted, tested, committed or otherwise disturbed. Unrelated private-platform changes are never included in an FEA slice.

Use the existing `runmat-types` numeric, shape, storage, layout, and residency vocabulary wherever its current semantics are already exact. Never read or disturb the separately owned active checkout. Use public dev lineage and owner-published contract facts; do not merge or cherry-pick unpublished platform work merely to obtain typed value, parallel, distributed or accelerator capabilities. If FEA later reaches a dependency on unpublished RM-1064 behavior, first look for independent analysis work. Only consider a direct integration checkpoint when its owning workstream declares it green and stable, confirms ancestry-preserving delivery to `dev`, and agrees on the shared contract surface.

The scaling material explicitly distinguishes local parallelism, independent task fanout, and cooperative distributed numerical work.

Optimization, sensitivity analysis, uncertainty quantification, topology optimization, nonlinear post-buckling, arbitrary user elements, and executable constitutive laws must be documented as future envelopes rather than implied capabilities. Documentation may describe the typed dependency and extension seams, but it must not present capability metadata as an implemented solver feature.

requirements.title: Runnable exact public documentation and limitations

obligations.criterion: A formulation is complete only when all of the following are true: Its public contract names the actual equations, procedure, assumptions, and supported envelope. Its identity is constructed only from a qualified pre-solve admission receipt and records exact spatial, temporal, constitutive, coupling, recovery, topology, source, and boundary realizations; identity validity is rechecked at persistence and decode boundaries. Canonical geometry, regions, materials, sources, boundaries, contacts, and interfaces are realized without heuristic substitution. Constraint kinds, targets, DOFs, values, frames, schedules, relations, and enforcement are strongly typed after document parsing. Signals, physical quantities, units, domains, interpolation, excitations, initial conditions, response spectra, and combination policies are strongly typed after document parsing or runtime-value admission. Every dependent procedure consumes an immutable compatible state through a typed semantic transition; step activation, continuation, branching, restart, and retry retain distinct meanings and identities. Prestressed and buckling procedures retain their converged base state, tangent/geometric-stiffness, load-pattern, constraint, contact, and linearization provenance. Callable-backed inputs are frozen, effect-checked, materialized, validated, content-addressed, and evidenced before solve; no live language callback executes inside assembly, solver iteration, or distributed rank logic. Explicit and generated inputs satisfy the same realization, conservation, identity, retry, placement-equivalence, and publication contracts. Constraint rank, null spaces, violations, reactions, work, and conflicts are verified and attributable to authored objects.

Its discrete formulation is implemented in one analysis-owned module hierarchy. All fields have correct units, locations, topology, and recovery semantics. Field, history, probe, reduction, monitor, and diagnostic requests have correct quantities, targets, locations, frames, sampling, retention, and cost admission. Result-field selection and observation evaluation remain separate from ordinary `plot` and `mesh` rendering. Its solver reports real residuals, increments, balances, and convergence. CPU and any claimed accelerator path execute the intended operator with honest fallback provenance. Numerical algorithms and preconditioners are selected from typed operator properties and reject incompatible combinations. Sparse pattern, numeric values, preparation, and reuse have separate validated identities and invalidation rules. Analytic/manufactured, patch, convergence, conservation, invalid-case, and independent-reference evidence passes governed tolerances. Coupled or adaptive variants demonstrate closure or target-quantity convergence. Every result has a satisfied typed accuracy report; failed or indeterminate mandatory evidence blocks publication. Progress, cancellation, retry, restart, replay, persistence, and result queries work. Inline, isolated-process, durable, and claimed remote execution meet the declared equivalence policy. Independent task distribution and cooperative distributed algebra have distinct lifecycle, retry, checkpoint, and failure semantics. Constraint-plan identity and mathematical behavior remain independent of mesh storage order, task partitioning, worker count, and placement.

Signal interpolation and excitation realization remain independent of task partitioning, worker count, and placement within the declared numerical-equivalence policy. Large numerical inputs, outputs, and checkpoints are chunked content-addressed artifacts with partial access; they are not gathered through the driver. Partitioned observations and reductions preserve values, locations, attribution, deterministic/tolerance policy, and bounded history semantics without unnecessary global field gathering. Resource-aware local execution does not oversubscribe its CPU, memory, or accelerator lease. Claimed GPU execution meets operation-level native-work, transfer, synchronization, precision, memory, and convergence gates. Performance and resource use satisfy the governed supported envelope. Public documentation contains runnable examples and exact limitations. Future parameter/sensitivity and compiled-law capability metadata is truthful and is not presented as implemented optimization, uncertainty, post-buckling, arbitrary-element, or arbitrary-material functionality. Blocking release evidence covers the formulation. The overall plan is complete only when every formulation in the planned production surface satisfies this definition and all obsolete proxy paths have been removed.

requirements.title: Per-formulation complete acceptance

obligations.criterion: For each implementation slice: Re-read the relevant section of the standing FEA acceptance specification and the current owning modules. State the intended domain owner and dependency direction before editing. Add or update a failing focused test or executable benchmark that expresses the required behavior. Implement the largest coherent vertical slice that can be designed, reviewed, and verified safely and productively; split only at a real domain, evidence, or risk boundary, and do not leave duplicate old/new behavior. Run formatting, focused tests, architecture checks, and relevant integration evidence. Use development telemetry for long-running or distributed work so progress and failures are inspected while execution is active. Review the diff for god-file growth, duplicate rules, misleading names, dead code, lint suppression, unrelated changes, and accidental work outside scope. Commit the measurable slice with a message describing the delivered behavior. Update the standing FEA acceptance specification only when evidence changes the dependency order, scope, or exit criteria. Never include unrelated changes from `runmat-private`, and never touch the separate active `runmat` checkout.

Each published example shows a verdict of passed, failed or indeterminate against its stated criteria with evidence in the results pane and CLI; an unconverged case returns indeterminate; `runmat reassess` re-evaluates criteria without re-solving.

`runmat snapshot` captures each hero study into a saved scene with the views the page shows: fields with cut planes and caps, field lines, arrows, isosurfaces, per-body transparency, AC-cycle playback, one view per frequency or mode, transient playback and streamlines, and the scene replays faithfully after save (NaN, colormaps, legends, units).
Guide and hero results save and cold-reopen in Desktop and the graphics-only web viewer with identical fields and views.
Repeated eigenvalues from symmetric sections do not degrade a modal run or block its snapshot.
Every result records the requested and actual backend, precision, solver method, preconditioner and any fallback stage, and a fallback never reports the requested backend as used.
The Desktop study editor, geometry viewer, results pane and agent pane operate on the published studies in the released app, with the same checks and results as the CLI.

tests.boundary: A loaded structural static study run through the CLI repeatedly and with explicit worker and thread counts (1x1, 4x1, 2x4) gives identical mesh identity, solver-state content digests and assessed scalar bits; one study, one platform.
tests.name: a_study_gives_identical_results_across_runs_workers_and_threads

obligations.criterion: The same study yields identical result digests across runs, thread counts and worker counts, with the guarantee and its scope (same build, hardware class) stated.

requirements.title: Results readable, verdicted and viewable

obligations.criterion: For every physics a table of named benchmark cases (analytic, manufactured and published) is generated from runs and published with the reference value, the computed value, the difference, mesh convergence and wall time, misses included; no value is typed by hand.
Formula, RunMat and an open solver agree within stated tolerance side by side on five real parts, with the method and any disagreement published.

The simulation docs, status tables and per-physics pages are generated from or checked against the admission registry and runner gate, and every row in the docs-drift list is closed; branch features are documented in the change that adds them.
The heat-sink and tuning-fork guides publish with their projects, archives and HTTP checks from accepted runs.
Each shippable physics family has a guide with a runnable example, including electrostatics, conduction, magnetostatics, harmonic Maxwell, acoustics and flow.

No `formulation = experimental` switch, maturity gate in admission or kernels, 'production qualification unsupported' rejection, or the word experimental in docs, examples and file names remains; a finished capability simply runs.

requirements.title: Validation published, docs true, no maturity surface

tests.boundary: Parses the checked-in inventory, rejects unmapped rows, duplicate ids and mappings to absent requirements or obligations; does not judge whether a mapping is sufficient.

requirements.title: The register defines done and maintains itself

obligations.criterion: Exactly one thread-plan authority binds the admitted cores for assembly, solve, recovery and publication of every family; no family reserves cores and runs serially, and a study that requests N threads is observed to use N.

Operator assembly, boundary and excitation realization, field recovery and publication run in parallel and agree with the serial reference within the declared tolerance, bit-for-bit where the policy declares it.
Direct (Cholesky, LDLT, LU), Krylov, AMG and block-eigen solves of the family run in parallel on the shared sparse layer and reproduce the serial solution and residual history within tolerance.
