obligations.criterion: The shared parallel kernels under every family agree with their serial references: element assembly into the sparse pattern is bit-identical to the serial loop at 1, 2, 3, 7 and 16 threads; scoped Krylov solves equal the serial solution and reject nested execution; pooled CSR products preserve serial bits and output shape.

tests.boundary: The loaded static box study gives bit-identical state digests and assessed values at serial and host-admissible parallel layouts (up to 8 total threads) through the public command; other families are not run.
tests.name: a_study_gives_identical_results_across_runs_workers_and_threads

obligations.criterion: The same study yields identical result digests, or differences within the stated tolerance, across 1, 2, 4 and all admitted threads.

A strong-scaling table from 1 to all cores of the stated machine, produced with the exclusive benchmark gate, is generated and published for the family's published example, with parallel efficiency and the hardware recorded.

requirements.title: Every family saturates the machine through one thread plan

obligations.criterion: `runmat run --cluster` runs the family's published study remotely with encrypted inputs, no unsupported-physics rejection, and results equal to the local run under the equivalence policy.

Sweep cases and independent frequency points run concurrently on local workers or a cluster, overlap in time, publish per-case status and return results in authored order identical to serial execution.

One problem partitions into owned and ghost subdomains over at least 4 workers; the cooperative solve equals the serial reference within tolerance, fails collectively with epoch fencing, and is demonstrated at a model size beyond one worker's memory share.
A long run checkpoints and restarts mid-phase after worker loss or cancellation to the same final result.

The shared remote, partitioned and thread-parallel contracts are one implementation reached by every family: no family-specific placement table, and unsupported placements fail typed before result commitment.

requirements.title: Remote and cooperative execution for every family

obligations.criterion: Each family solves a model of at least one million degrees of freedom (cells for flow) through the public command within a stated wall time and memory, on stated hardware, with the result checked against the same reference as the small case.
For every physics page example the node count, degrees of freedom, wall time, peak memory and hardware are generated from the run and published.

Whole-task peak resident memory is measured across worker processes and compared with the admitted estimate; admission never over-reserves a practical small model (buckling at 3,000 nodes, modal output, blade) and never admits a model that then exceeds its bound.

The plan reports cores, memory, wall time and core hours before a run; each run records per-stage usage and classifies failures (resource, numerical, input, infrastructure) in typed form, and the stated core-hour figure per guide is measured on the release.

Steady flow on 1 million cells on a 16-core workstation completes in under 3 minutes and 4 GB, 10 million cells in under 45 minutes and 40 GB; transient flow sustains at least 2 million cell-steps per second per CPU node; strong-scaling efficiency is at least 70 percent down to 50,000 cells per core.

requirements.title: Millions of degrees of freedom at stated time and memory

obligations.criterion: A shell panel (MITC3, homogeneous and laminate layups with orthotropic plies) and a beam frame (general, rectangular, circular and tube sections) run from a `.fea` study on imported geometry and publish results; a plate matches the plate-bending formula, a frame matches beam theory, and a frame with code limits written as assessments returns verdicts.

Every structural load the docs list runs and conserves its resultant: total, distributed and remote-point forces, moments and torque, traction, pressure (wind, mapped from a fluid result, hydrostatic), gravity and body force, inertial and centrifugal acceleration, base acceleration and earthquake motion, bolt preload, bearing loads on holes, thermal expansion, line loads, harmonic amplitudes, load cases and combinations, and local coordinate systems.

Fixed supports, prescribed motion, couplings, ties, periodic constraints, equations, axial springs and dashpots, point springs to ground, elastic foundations, six-DOF bushings, rotational springs, nonlinear springs and gaps, frequency-dependent mounts and bonded interfaces run with reactions that balance the loads, and no weak spring, mass, damping, reference constraint or load case is added silently.
A `structural nonlinear` cantilever under a tip load to large rotation matches the elastica solution with Newton and load stepping.
A published J2 plasticity example (linear isotropic hardening, follower loads) runs and matches the manufactured or analytic reference including unloading.
A published frictionless and Coulomb contact example (bolted bracket) runs from the public command and matches a Hertz or sliding reference.

Cantilever tip deflection matches PL^3/(3EI) (0.199 against 0.200 mm), the first bending frequency matches Euler-Bernoulli (81.3 against 81.5 Hz), and a random-vibration study matches Miles' equation, with the coarse-mesh failure (0.1197 mm Tet4) flagged as cannot-tell rather than accepted.

A random-response study driven by a PSD (GEVS-type) from modal data reports RMS and 3-sigma stress, matching an independent modal combination.
